L664@P20: Exemption (f) - The Investigatory Exemption
L665@P20: Exemption (f), the investigatory exemption, provides custodians a basis for
L666@P20: withholding:
L667@P20: investigatory materials necessarily compiled out of the public view by
L668@P20: law enforcement or other investigatory officials the disclosure of which
L669@P20: materials would probably so prejudice the possibility of effective law
L670@P20: enforcement that such disclosure would not be in the public interest.80
L671@P20: The exemption allows investigative officials to withhold materials that could
L672@P20: compromise investigative efforts if disclosed. Exemption (f) does not,
L673@P20: however, create a blanket exemption for all records that investigative officials
L674@P20: create or maintain.81 A custodian of records generally must demonstrate a
L675@P20: prejudice to investigative efforts in order to withhold requested records.
L676@P20: Information relating to an ongoing investigation may be withheld if disclosure
L677@P20: could alert suspects to the activities of investigative officials. Confidential
L678@P20: investigative techniques may also be withheld indefinitely if disclosure is
L679@P20: deemed to be prejudicial to future law enforcement activities.82
L680@P20: Redactions may be appropriate where they serve to preserve the anonymity of
L681@P20: voluntary witnesses.83 Exemption (f) invites a “case-by-case consideration” of
L682@P20: whether disclosure “would probably so prejudice the possibility of effective
L683@P20: law enforcement that such disclosure would not be in the public interest.”84
L684@P20: For example: If a requested incident report contains witness identities, can a
L685@P20: police department use Exemption (f) to withhold the requested report in its
L686@P20: entirety?
L687@P20: Generally, a police incident report may be released to a requestor after the
L688@P20: records custodian has redacted the exempt portions from the record, such as,
L689@P20: medical information and information that may identify a voluntary witness.

L695@P20: information submitted as required by law or as a condition of receiving

L1117@P34: The Records Management Unit (RMU) was created to provide records
L1118@P34: management services and outreach to all state agencies and municipalities to
L1119@P34: help them meet state record-keeping standards and requirements. The RMU
L1120@P34: can provide agencies with retention schedules for specific records, as well as
L1121@P34: information on proper disposal and destruction of records. If you need
L1122@P34: additional information or assistance in creating a Records Management
L1123@P34: Program, please contact the RMU at 617-727-2816.
L1124@P34: Records Retention
L1125@P34: It is the responsibility of government employees who create, receive and
L1126@P34: maintain public records to ensure their safekeeping and availability to the
L1127@P34: public until the retention period for the specific records series has expired.
L1128@P34: There are two retention schedules: the Municipal Records Retention Schedule,
L1129@P34: which applies to all records of municipal government in Massachusetts, and
L1130@P34: the Statewide Schedule, which applies to all records of state agencies
L1131@P34: including those of executive departments, constitutional offices, authorities,
L1132@P34: independent agencies, and state records being managed by contracted service
L1133@P34: providers.
L1134@P34: State agencies must obtain the written permission of the Records Conservation
L1135@P34: Board (RCB) prior to destroying certain records.128 The RCB is empowered
L1136@P34: “to require all departments of the Commonwealth to report to it what series of
L1137@P34: records they hold, to set standards for the management and preservation of
L1138@P34: such records, and to establish schedules for the destruction, in whole, or in
L1139@P34: part, and transfer to the archives or another appropriate division within the
L1140@P34: office of the state secretary, in whole, or in part, of records no longer needed
L1141@P34: for current business.”129
L1183@P36: The Supervisor of Records is responsible for ensuring that the records of the
L1184@P36: Commonwealth and municipalities are maintained and stored as required by
L1185@P36: law.134 In accordance with this duty, the following procedures have been
L1186@P36: established to ensure security of and access to public records.
L1187@P36: 1. Records Access Officers (RAOs)
L1188@P36: RAOs shall assist the custodian in preserving public records in
L1189@P36: accordance with all applicable laws, rules, regulations and retention
L1190@P36: schedules.135
L1191@P36: 2. Original Records Removed from Municipal Offices
L1192@P36: a. Whenever original public records are removed from municipal
L1193@P36: offices for use in the regular course of business to a private office
L1194@P36: or home, they shall be stored in fire-resistant devices and safes
L1195@P36: provided by the municipality.136
L1196@P36: b. If fire-resistant storage outside of the municipal building cannot be
L1197@P36: ensured, then no original records may be removed. However, the
L1198@P36: RAO may create copies of records for use in a private office or
L1199@P36: home.
L1200@P36: 3. Original Records Created Outside of Municipal Offices
L1201@P36: a. Whenever original public records are created outside the municipal
L1202@P36: offices, they shall be transferred on a regular and frequent basis to
L1203@P36: secure storage in the municipal building.
L1204@P36: b. If secure storage is available in an individual’s private office or
L1205@P36: home, then copies of the records shall be maintained in the
L1206@P36: municipal building, with the originals stored in secure storage at
L1207@P36: the records custodian’s private office or home.

L338@P10: Fees for Copies
L339@P10: In addition to the search and segregation fees, records custodians may charge
L340@P10: $0.05 for either single and double-sided black and white paper copies or
L341@P10: printouts.30 When the request is for materials that are not susceptible to
L342@P10: ordinary means of reproduction, such as photographs or computer tapes, the
L343@P10: actual cost of reproduction may be assessed to the requestor.31 There are also
L344@P10: specific statutes that establish fees for copies of public records.32
L345@P10: Agencies
L346@P10: Agencies may not assess a fee for the first 4 hours of time spent searching for,
L347@P10: compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record.
L348@P10: Agencies may not assess a fee of more than $25 per hour for the cost to
L349@P10: comply with a request for public records.33
L350@P10: Municipalities
L351@P10: Municipalities with a population of over 20,000 may not assess a fee for the
L352@P10: first 2 hours of time spent searching for, compiling, segregating, redacting and
L353@P10: reproducing a requested record. Municipalities with a population of 20,000
L354@P10: and under may assess a fee, including the first 2 hours, for time spent
L355@P10: searching for, compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested
L356@P10: record.34
L357@P10: Population data shall be determined by the decennial US. Census and it shall
L358@P10: be the burden of the RAO to provide population data information when
L359@P10: responding to a request.35
L360@P10: A municipality may not assess a fee of more than $25 per hour for the cost to

L364@P11: Remedies for Requestors
L365@P11: Supervisor of Records
L366@P11: If a records custodian denies access to, or cannot produce requested records in
L367@P11: 10 business days, the records custodian is still required by statute to provide a
L368@P11: response in accordance with G. L. c. 66, § 10(b) within 10 business days. The
L369@P11: custodian must also inform the requestor of the right of appeal to the
L370@P11: Supervisor under G. L. c. 66, § 10(A)(a).37 A requestor who is denied access
L371@P11: to any requested information may petition the Supervisor for an appeal of the
L372@P11: response, or lack thereof, within 90 days.38
L373@P11: The Supervisor, assisted by Public Records Division staff, then reviews the
L374@P11: written request, the custodian’s written response, and provides a written ruling
L375@P11: on the status of the records or the reasonableness of a fee estimate.
L376@P11: The Supervisor must issue a determination within 10 business days of receipt
L377@P11: of the appeal.39 If a custodian does not comply with an order, the Supervisor
L378@P11: may notify the Office of the Attorney General for enforcement.40
L379@P11: The Supervisor and the Public Records Division staff provide training by
L380@P11: request to public entities and associations of public employees seeking
L381@P11: information on the proper application of the Public Records Law to its
L382@P11: records. Public Records Division staff will answer questions on the phone
L383@P11: informally, both from requestors and from government entities.
L384@P11: You may view determinations issued by the Supervisor since 2014 on the
L385@P11: Public Records Division website at:
L386@P11: http://www.sec.state.ma.us/appealsweb/appealsstatus.aspx.
L387@P11: Superior Court
L388@P11: Notwithstanding the ability to appeal to the Supervisor, a requestor may
L389@P11: initiate a civil action to enforce the requirements of the Public Records Law.
L390@P11: Under the updated Public Records Law, the superior court may award
L391@P11: reasonable attorney fees and costs in certain circumstances.41

L2041@P61: 32.04 : Records Access Officers
L2042@P61: (1) Each agency and municipality shall designate one or more employees as
L2043@P61: records access officer(s).
L2044@P61: (2) In a municipality, the municipal clerk, or the clerk's designees, or any
L2045@P61: designee of a municipality that the chief executive officer of the municipality
L2046@P61: may appoint, shall serve as records access officers.
L2047@P61: (3) The designation of a records access officer shall not be construed to
L2048@P61: prohibit employees who have been previously authorized by the agency or
L2049@P61: municipality to make public records or information available to the public
L2050@P61: from continuing to do so in accordance with 950 CMR 32.00.
L2051@P61: (4) Each agency and municipality shall post in a conspicuous location at its
L2052@P61: offices and on its website, if any, the name, title, business address, business
L2053@P61: telephone number, and business email address of each records access officer.
L2054@P61: (5) A records access officer shall:
L2055@P61: (a) coordinate the custodian's response to requests for access to public
L2056@P61: records and shall facilitate the resolution of such requests by the timely
L2057@P61: and thorough production of public records;
L2058@P61: (b) assist persons seeking public records to identify the records
L2059@P61: sought;
L2060@P61: (c) assist the custodian in preserving public records in accordance
L2061@P61: with all applicable laws, rules, regulations and retention schedules;
